first.rationale: Prioritize an onboarding-simplification experiment to address the observed completion decline and restore durable self-serve adoption. Verify the prior onboarding result and the pricing-retention tradeoff before committing; aggressive pricing may counter the competitor but has known long-term retention risk.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding for self-serve accounts. Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and verified prior evidence shows a shortened flow increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; signup simplification independently improved SMB activation. This directly addresses the current funnel deterioration with evidence of sustainable downstream value. Do not use promotional pricing: verified results show the apparent revenue gain was offset by a 12% 30-day retention decline and failure to survive the first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: Keep the committed onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses falling onboarding completion and activation with verified evidence of higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved retention. The deeper competitor cut and increased SMB churn raise urgency, but do not overturn the verified finding that targeted promotional pricing produces short-lived revenue and materially harms retention through renewal. Pricing pressure is a material risk to monitor, not sufficient evidence that an unsustainable discount is the best use of this cycle's single experiment.
